content: The Sommelet reaction is a specific type of organic chemical reaction in which a benzyl halide is transformed into an aldehyde. This transformation occurs through the action of hexamine (also known as hexamethylenetetramine) and water. A reaction that is conceptually similar to the Sommelet reaction is the Duff reaction, where the benzyl halide is replaced by an arene as the starting material. In the Kröhnke aldehyde synthesis, the oxidizing agent used is a combination of pyridine and p-nitrosodimethylaniline. This reaction represents another method for synthesizing aldehydes, utilizing a distinct set of reagents and conditions.
